items.stem: A feed that should return 65,000 students has a bug and returns 0 records. What feature prevents the destination's entire student set from being garbage-collected (deleted)?

options.text: Delta detection
A garbage-collection / deletion percentage abort threshold
The duplication key
Resumability

items.explanation: The GC/deletion percentage threshold compares the would-be deletions (all 65,000) against the destination count; exceeding the configured % aborts the run.

misconceptions.a: Delta detection would faithfully conclude everything was deleted — the threshold is the guard that stops it.
misconceptions.d: Resumability handles crashes, not bad data volumes.

options.text: Runs always complete faster on the second attempt
If the server crashes mid-run, no data is lost and the next run picks up where it left off
The destination is backed up before every run
Exceptions are automatically retried forever

items.explanation: Because progress is recorded in StarBridge, a crash mid-run causes no data loss; the next run resumes from where it stopped.

misconceptions.c: Resumability is about safe continuation, not backups.

items.stem: If the deletion-percentage threshold parameter is omitted from configuration, what is assumed?

options.text: 0% — no deletions are ever allowed
100% — full deletion is allowed (no deletion guard)
5% by default
The run will not start

items.explanation: An omitted percentage is assumed to be 100%, meaning the destination entity could be fully deleted — the guard only protects you if you configure it.

misconceptions.a: It defaults to permissive (100%), not restrictive (0%).

items.stem: What is the difference between the SegmentAbortThreshold and the RunAbortThreshold?

options.text: One counts exceptions within a single segment; the other is the limit across the whole run
One is for deletions; the other is for creations
They are the same thing with different names
One applies to the source; the other to the destination

items.explanation: SegmentAbortThreshold aborts a single segment after N exceptions; RunAbortThreshold is the overall exception limit for the entire run.

items.stem: Thresholds exist because delta detection trusts the snapshot. What is the best one-sentence framing of what thresholds are?

options.text: A way to make runs finish faster
Guardrails against a bad snapshot, so a faulty feed can't silently wreck the destination
A logging feature for the dashboard
A replacement for mappings

items.explanation: Because the engine acts on whatever snapshot the feed provides, thresholds are the safety guardrails that abort the run when the snapshot implies dangerous, large-scale change.
